newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British Business press - Oct 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British Business press - Oct 2.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- ROVER'S NEW LEASE OF LIFE FOR MINI

BMW announced at the Paris motor show yesterday that it will go ahead with a new version of the Mini, ending speculation that the 37-year-old model has finally reached the end of the road. The new mini will be built in Britain by Rover but the engines will be imported from a South American plant built by BMW in association with Chrysler, the American car group.
-- LIMELIGHT HEADS FOR MARKET WITH 170 MILLION POUNDS STG PRICE TAG

Limelight is to float on the Stock Exchange with an expected valuation of 170 million pounds stg. The Moben kitchens to Dolphin bathrooms group is expected to issue a pathfinder prospectus later this month. The float is not expected to raise any funds for the company but it could realise about 60 million pounds stg for Stephen Boler, the entrepreneur who created the group. Boler is likely to reduce his stake in the company to between 15 and 20 per cent, from 49 percent.
-- NORWICH UNION TO ANNOUNCE 4 BILLION POUNDS STG FLOTATION

Norwich Union will this morning announce its long awaited plans for a 4 billion pounds stg stock market flotation. When Norwich Union becomes the first British insurer to shed mutual status, some 3 million policyholders will receive windfall bonuses worth at least 500 pounds stg each. For the float to proceed it must be supported by a simple voting majority of Norwich Union's with- profits policyholders.
THE TIMES
-- BRANSON SETS 1998 TARGET FOR CITY-HEATHROW RAIL LINK

The proposed rail link between the City and Heathrow airport could be in operation by 1998 providing the project gets the go ahead from the British Airports Authority later this month. The 50 million pounds stg fast rail link, backed by Richard Branson's Virgin Group, would need no public subsidy and already has the approval of Railtrack. Approval by the BAA board is one of the last major hurdles standing in the way of the service which would take passengers from Heathrow to Moorgate in the heart of the City in 36 minutes.
-- HOUSE OF FRASER TO SHUT SHOPS AS LOSSES GROW

House of Fraser is to shut up to ten stores in an attempt to improve its financial performance. The department store group revealed its plans yesterday after reporting worse than expected half-year losses of 13.6 million pounds stg. The final decision on the closure or sale of between five and ten of its underperforming stores has yet to be taken.
-- BP JOINS IN 230 MILLION POUNDS STG PROJECT TO REDEVELOP PORT TALBOT

A redevelopment programme of Port Talbot could create 3,000 new jobs over ten years. BP Chemicals, the Welsh Development Agency and Neath Port Talbot County Council have joined forces to launch the 230 million pounds stg redevelopment which will concentrate on establishing Wales's first Energy Park alongside BP's premises at Port Talbot. The park will then be marketed as an inward investment location for environmentally friendly businesses.
THE GUARDIAN
-- EUROTUNNEL ON BRINK OF SEALING SURVIVAL DEAL

Eurotunnel are on the verge of clinching the rescheduling of its 8 billion pounds stg debt and avoiding the threat of being dragged into administration under French law. Leading bankers are hopeful that an agreement will be reached by the end of the week. Members of the 220 strong banking consortium are expected to announce that a deal has been reached in principle.
-- MoD SUED OVER ATOMIC PLANT 'CONTAMINATION'

The Ministry of Defence have had a multi-million pound damages claim brought against them by industrial group, Blue Circle. The industrial group claims that the Atomic Weapons Establishment contaminated its land with nuclear materials and rendered it unsaleable. High levels of plutonium and uranium were allegedly found on Blue Circle's estate next to the AWE plant at Aldermaston, Berkshire, where the Trident warhead is made.
-- TOBACCO CASES FAIL TO DAMAGE IMPERIAL'S STOCK MARKET RETURN

Shares in Imperial Tobacco, the first of the four companies being demerged from Hanson, closed yesterday at 392.5p against their issue price of 375p, despite fears over litigation after last week's decision by 40 smokers to file an action against Imperial. The company is now valued at just over 2
billion pounds stg.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- CASH-RICH INVESTORS HELP PUSH FOOTSIE NEARER 4,000 MARK

New figures from purchasing managers confirming the strength of the recovery in industry helped push the FTSE 100 index to an all time closing high last night of 3,992.2, up 38.5 on the day. Analysts are predicting that the index could soon rise above the 4,000 level. Cash-rich institutions are ignoring warnings from fund managers PDFM that the stock market is ready to crash, and are stepping up their share purchases.
-- SAINSBURY MOVES INTO FINANCIAL SERVICES

Sainsbury's is getting ready to launch a series of initiatives including a move into financial services between now and Christmas, in a bid to win back market share lost to rivals. Financial services offered are likely to include a "bank account" similar to Tesco's ClubCard Plus scheme. They also plan to emphasise Sainsbury's strengths such as quality, choice and customer service, and take the attention away from price.
-- ELISABETH MURDOCH ASSUMES CONTROL AT BSKYB

The daughter of media baron Rupert Murdoch is to take charge of all programming at BSkyB. Elisabeth Murdoch will oversee BSkyB's growing programming division as well as continue in her role as general manager of broadcasting. The extension of her position brings her a step closer to the mantle of heir-apparent at her father's global empire.
